items.item_text: Bachelor's degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training.
Master's degree in related area or equivalent experience/training.
6 - 10 years of related experience.
Project management experience.
Experience supporting diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives within a higher education environment.

Manages, plans, and administers a full range of administrative operations in a small to medium academic department, or a small to medium non-academic department or program, where operations are significantly complex in terms of budgetary funding, number of faculty, staff and students, and/or are broad in scope due to focus of operations (e.g., computer or wet lab space and equipment, fundraising, grant writing, etc.). (55% time)

Oversees the scheduling and management of all meeting and travel schedules for the VC-DEI, as well as any conference or professional travel for other ODEI staff members, on rare occasions for committee member participation, and visiting dignitaries. Steps in as the designee often as needed. Functions as the initial point of contact for government officials, UCOP administrators, national professional association leaders, community organizations, business leaders, and community members regarding the ODEI and local issues. Consults with senior leaders, managers, and professional staff to identify problems, develop improvements, and create and maintain quality standards. Participates in meetings with the Vice Chancellor to provide supporting information on the subject matter, including creation of shared drives, meeting notes, archives, inventories, etc. Attends operational meetings to keep abreast of plans, projects, decisions, problems, etc., about the organization's various functions. (15% time)

Performs administrative operations activities as predominant focus of position, with accountability for operational and budget processes, staff FTE, finance, human resources and space planning. (10% time)

Develops analysis, special reports, detailed briefings, agendas, and presentations for the Vice Chancellor for other internal and external officials and directs the preparation of reports for meetings outside the organization by ensuring that updates and the appropriate information has been gathered and reviewed for the Vice Chancellor's use. Initiates recommendations for improved procedures for greater efficiency and effectiveness of the organization. Develops concise, clear executive briefing documents and talking points on a given topic or campus event hosted by the ODEI for the Chancellor, Provost, and other campus leaders to acquaint them with public officials, donors, and community leaders, as well as critical issues to consider in planning and managing their participation Ensures tracking of comprehensive ODEI Strategic Planning goals and implementation for the office and the campus. (10% time)
Typically supervises support staff or small number of professional staff within or outside the scope of main business activities (e.g., student services, facilities, etc.). (5% time)

Initiates tactful inquiries on behalf of the Vice Chancellor regarding the disposition, conduct, progress or resolution of sensitive issues and matters of confidential nature. Briefs and debriefs the Vice Chancellor on politically and academically sensitive issues with a deep and sensitive awareness of the short- and long-range goals/objectives of the ODEI. (5% time)

Advanced knowledge of financial analysis and reporting techniques, and/or human resources policies and procedures for staff and academic employees.
Advanced knowledge of University rules and regulations, processes, protocols and procedures for budget, accounting and fund management, and/or personnel management.

Advanced knowledge of a variety of administrative operational activities such as events planning, basic fundraising processes, risk management planning, website design, accounting and payroll, travel and reimbursements, and contracts and grants regulations and guidelines.
Advanced knowledge of common University-specific computer application programs.
Advanced interpersonal communication skills to include verbal and written, active listening, critical thinking, persuasiveness, advising and counseling skills.
Demonstrated project management skills, including the ability to coordinate complex initiatives, manage competing priorities, and meet established deadlines.
Advanced skills in short and long term strategic planning, analysis and problem-solving and customer service.
Ability to use discretion and maintain confidentiality.
